# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for a test run of the AMG2023 benchmark
# on an AWS ARM-based CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster.
# It configures a single-node Flux cluster to run a small problem size.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A unique name for the MiniCluster instance to avoid collisions.
  name: amg-test-3
  # Deployment will be in the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for the initial test.
  size: 1

  # Do not automatically clean up pods after completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict logging for detailed output.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific options tailored for an ARM architecture environment.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture to ensure compatibility.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Define the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The launcher flag MUST be false for the main application container.
      # The Flux Operator injects its own launcher pod.
      launcher: false
      # The command to execute. Flux will wrap this with the necessary MPI bootstrap commands.
      # Runs AMG problem 2 with a small processor grid (-P 4 4 4) for testing.
      command: amg -problem 2 -P 4 4 4
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      # This ensures the pod is scheduled on a node with an EFA device.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest addresses the previous failure by aligning
# the number of tasks with the application's requirements and setting
# necessary environment variables for EFA networking on AWS.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A unique name for the MiniCluster instance to avoid collisions.
  name: amg-test-4
  # Deployment will be in the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster remains 1 for this test.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. This MUST match the processor grid.
  # For -P 4 4 4, the total tasks are 4 * 4 * 4 = 64.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not automatically clean up pods after completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict logging for detailed output.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific options for an ARM architecture and performance.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture to ensure compatibility.
    arch: "arm"
    # Adds Flux option flags, here for CPU affinity which is crucial for performance.
    optionFlags: "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Define the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The launcher flag MUST be false for the main application container.
      launcher: false
      # The command to execute. Flux will wrap this with the necessary MPI bootstrap commands.
      # Runs AMG problem 2 with a 4x4x4 processor grid, requiring 64 tasks.
      command: amg -problem 2 -P 4 4 4

      # Environment variables for OpenMPI (OMPI) and Libfabric (FI) to correctly
      # utilize the AWS EFA network interface for low-latency communication.
      environment:
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_pml: "cm"
        OMPI_MCA_mtl: "ofi"
        FI_PROVIDER: "efa"
        FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: "cma"

      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      # This ensures the pod is scheduled on a node with an EFA device.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
